description: A bottom drawer with a close button, swipe handle and footer for focused tasks such as editing a profile.
overview:
`Modal` wraps `Drawer` with the swipe handle turned on, and `ModalContent` shows a close button by default. It slides up from the bottom of the screen and can be swiped down or closed with the button.

Use it for a self-contained task, such as a short form, that the user completes or cancels before returning to the screen.
usage:
Wrap a button in `ModalTrigger`, then put a `ModalHeader`, `ModalBody` and `ModalFooter` inside `ModalContent`. `ModalFooter` stacks its buttons in reverse order, so the first button in code appears at the bottom.

The modal can be uncontrolled or controlled with `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange`. Pass `showCloseButton={false}` on `ModalContent` to hide the close button.

examples.OpenByDefault: Opens the modal on first render with `defaultOpen`.
examples.Floating: Detaches the drawer from the screen edges with `floating`.

parts.Modal: The root drawer with a swipe handle.
parts.ModalTrigger: The element that opens the modal.
parts.ModalContent: The sliding panel, with a close button by default.
parts.ModalBody: A padded container for the main content.
parts.ModalFooter: A vertical, reverse-ordered stack of buttons.
parts.ModalClose: An element that closes the modal.

Modal.open: Controls whether the modal is open.
Modal.defaultOpen: Whether the modal starts open when uncontrolled.
Modal.onOpenChange: Called when the modal opens or closes.
Modal.floating: Insets the drawer from the screen edges.

ModalContent.showCloseButton: Shows the close button. Defaults to `true`.

notes: - Content respects the safe area insets.
